exercises.title: Filtering 1: Towns with greater than 150,000 people
Filtering 2: Towns with greater than 150,000 people and in Oregon
exercises.solution:
SELECT town, state, population_2020_census 
  FROM pnw_towns 
 WHERE population_2020_census > 150000
   AND state = 'Oregon';

exercises.title: Filtering 3: Towns with greater than 150,000 people or in Oregon
exercises.solution:
SELECT town, state, population_2020_census 
  FROM pnw_towns 
 WHERE population_2020_census > 150000
    OR state = 'Oregon';

exercises.title: Filtering 4: Counties established after 1920 with a population greater than 100,000
exercises.solution:

  FROM pnw_counties

exercises.title: Filtering 5: Counties established after 1880 with a population greater than 100,000

exercises.title: Filtering 6: Towns with a land area between 12 and 15 square miles
exercises.solution:
SELECT town, state, land_area_sq_mi
  FROM pnw_towns
 WHERE land_area_sq_mi >= 12
   AND land_area_sq_mi <= 15;

exercises.title: Filtering 7: Towns with a land area between 10 and 15 square miles (simplified)
Filtering 8: Counties in Washington established between 1890 and 1900 or counties in Oregon with a population greater than 300,000 in 2022
exercises.solution:
SELECT county, state, year_established, population_2022
  FROM pnw_counties
 WHERE (state = 'Washington' AND year_established BETWEEN 1890 AND 1900)
    OR (state = 'Oregon' AND population_2022 > 300000);

exercises.title: Transforming 1: Classifying towns by population size using CASE WHEN
exercises.solution:
SELECT town, 
       population_2010_census,
       CASE 
           WHEN population_2010_census > 100000 THEN 'Large'
           WHEN population_2010_census BETWEEN 50000 AND 100000 THEN 'Medium'
           ELSE 'Small'
       END AS town_size
  FROM pnw_towns
  ORDER BY population_2010_census DESC;

Joining 1: Get population of each county seat
Joining 2: Show ALL counties, even those whose seat isn't in our towns data
Joining 3: Find counties that don't have any towns listed
exercises.solution:
SELECT c.county
 FROM pnw_counties AS c
LEFT JOIN pnw_towns AS t ON c.county = t.primary_county
WHERE t.town IS NULL;

Filtering Techniques
Select Boeing Planes' Tail Numbers and Models
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query selects tail numbers and models of planes manufactured by Boeing.
SELECT tailnum, model 
FROM planes 
WHERE manufacturer = 'BOEING';

exercises.title: Select airports (faa, name, lat) above 40 latitude and in the America/New_York time zone.
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query selects certain columns from airports based on specified conditions.
SELECT faa, name, lat 
FROM airports 
WHERE lat > 40 
AND tzone = 'America/New_York';

exercises.title: Select airports (faa code, name, and lat) within 40 to 42 degrees latitude.
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query selects FAA codes, names, and latitudes of airports within a specific latitude range.
SELECT faa, name, lat 
FROM airports 
WHERE lat BETWEEN 40 AND 42;

exercises.title: Select airlines (carrier code and name) with name starting with an "A"
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query selects the carrier code and name of airlines with names starting with 'A'.
SELECT carrier, name 
FROM airlines 
WHERE name LIKE 'A%';

exercises.title: Select flights having 101 as the second, third, and fourth characters of the tail number.
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query selects flights with tail numbers that have '101' as the second, third, and fourth characters.
SELECT tailnum 
FROM flights 
WHERE tailnum LIKE '_101%';

exercises.title: Select flights (all columns) where the carrier is either "AS" or "HA"
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query selects all flights where the carrier is either "AS" or "HA".
SELECT * 
FROM flights 
WHERE carrier IN ('AS', 'HA');

exercises.title: Group flights by origin and calculate the average arrival delay as `avg_arr_delay`
exercises.solution:

exercises.title: Group flights by destination and count the number of flights for each destination having more than 100 flights as `total_flights`
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query groups flights by destination and counts the number of flights for each, only including those destinations with more than 100 flights.
SELECT dest, COUNT(*) AS total_flights
FROM flights
GROUP BY dest
HAVING COUNT(*) > 100;

exercises.title: Transforming Techniques
Categorize flights by distance as Short, Medium, or Long. Use 'Short' for distances less than 500 miles, 'Medium' for 500 to 2000 miles, and 'Long' for more than 2000 miles.
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query categorizes flights by distance as 'Short', 'Medium', or 'Long'.
SELECT distance, CASE 
WHEN distance < 500 THEN 'Short'
WHEN distance BETWEEN 500 AND 2000 THEN 'Medium'
ELSE 'Long'
END AS flight_distance_category
FROM flights;

exercises.title: Calculate the average speed of flights grouped by origin and destination and order by the fastest average speed
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query calculates the average speed of flights from each origin to each destination and orders the results by the fastest average speeds.
SELECT origin, dest,
AVG(distance / (air_time / 60)) AS avg_speed
FROM flights
GROUP BY origin, dest
ORDER BY avg_speed DESC;

exercises.title: Joining Techniques
Join flights (as `f`) with weather (as `w`) on `origin` and `time_hour` (returning only the rows matching between both tables). Select the `origin`, `dest`,
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query joins the flights table with the weather table on matching origin and time_hour, selecting origin, destination, temperature, and humidity.
SELECT f.origin, f.dest, w.temp, w.humid
FROM flights AS f
INNER JOIN weather AS w ON f.origin = w.origin AND f.time_hour = w.time_hour;

exercises.title: Left join flights with planes on tailnum (returning all rows from flights and only the rows from planes that match). Select the `tailnum`, `origin`, `dest`, `manufacturer`, and `model` fields.
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query left joins the flights table with the planes table on matching tailnum, selecting tailnum, origin, destination, manufacturer, and model.
SELECT f.tailnum, f.origin, f.dest, p.manufacturer, p.model
FROM flights AS f
LEFT JOIN planes AS p ON f.tailnum = p.tailnum;

exercises.title: Anti-join flights (as `f`) with planes (as `p`) where plane's tailnum is missing. Select the `tailnum`, `origin`, and `dest` fields.
exercises.solution:
-- SOLUTION: This query left joins the flights table with the planes table on matching tailnum, selecting flights' tailnum, origin, and destination where the corresponding tailnum in planes is missing.
SELECT f.tailnum, f.origin, f.dest
FROM flights AS f
LEFT JOIN planes AS p ON f.tailnum = p.tailnum
WHERE p.tailnum IS NULL;
